actors.title: Google Trends Scraper: Unlimited Keywords + Daily Data
actors.description: Google Trends without its limits: compare up to 100 keywords on one 0-100 scale (Google stops at 5), and daily data for any range, even 5 years or 2004-now (Google gives weekly/monthly). Plus regions, related queries and Trending Now. Paced so runs finish.
useFor: Google Trends interest over time, interest by region, related queries for keywords
compare more than 5 keywords on one 0-100 scale (up to 100)
daily Google Trends data for long ranges (12 months, 5 years, 2004-now)
what is trending on Google right now in a country (Trending Now)
replacement for pytrends when it fails with 429 TooManyRequestsError
pricing: $0.003 per trends report (trends-report): One Explore report: interest over time, interest by region and related queries for up to 5 compared terms.
$0.0005 per trending search (trending-item): One trending search from Trending Now, with volume, growth, related searches and category.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.title: What to scrape
inputs.description: Explore gives interest over time, by region and related queries for your search terms. Trending Now lists every search trending in the countries you pick.
enumTitles: Explore: search terms (interest over time, by region, related queries)
Trending Now: what's trending in a country right now

inputs.name: searchTerms
inputs.title: Search terms
inputs.description: One report per line. Compare terms by separating them with commas, e.g. coffee, tea. No 5-term limit: put up to 100 terms on one line and they all come back on one 0-100 scale (Google itself compares only 5; we chain overlapping groups, charged per Google query used). You can also paste a Google Trends explore URL, and its terms, country, time range and category are used as-is.

inputs.name: geo
inputs.title: Country or region
inputs.description: ISO country code like US, AU, GB, or a region like US-CA. Leave empty for worldwide.

inputs.name: timeRange
inputs.title: Time range
inputs.description: Period to analyse. Google picks the resolution: minutes for the past hour or 4 hours, hours for 7 days, days up to 90 days, weeks up to 5 years, and months since 2004.

inputs.name: customTimeRange
inputs.title: Custom time range (optional)
inputs.description: Overrides the time range above. Format YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2024-01-01 2024-06-30.

inputs.name: dailyData
inputs.title: Daily data for any time range
inputs.description: Google only gives daily points for ranges under ~9 months, then weekly or monthly. Turn this on to get daily points for the whole range (12 months, 5 years, even 2004 to now): we fetch ~8-month daily windows and scale each one to Google's full-range series. Each window is one more Google query, charged as a report (5 years ≈ 10 reports). Up to 5 terms per line.

inputs.name: category
inputs.title: Category ID
inputs.description: Google Trends category, e.g. 0 = all, 71 = Food & Drink, 7 = Finance. Default 0.

inputs.name: searchProperty
inputs.title: Search type
inputs.description: Which Google search to measure: web (default), images, news, Google Shopping or YouTube.

inputs.name: interestOverTime
inputs.title: Interest over time
inputs.description: Relative search interest (0-100) over the chosen time range.

inputs.name: interestByRegion
inputs.title: Interest by region
inputs.description: Relative search interest (0-100) by country, region, city or US metro area.

inputs.name: relatedQueries
inputs.title: Related queries (top + rising)
inputs.description: The top and rising searches related to each term, including "Breakout" queries (growth over 5,000%).

inputs.name: regionResolution
inputs.title: Region resolution
inputs.description: Level of detail for interest by region. "Google default" uses countries for worldwide and regions within a country.

inputs.name: includeLowVolumeRegions
inputs.title: Include low search volume regions
inputs.description: Include regions with too little search volume for Google to rate reliably (they usually show 0).

inputs.name: saveCsv
inputs.title: Also save spreadsheet-friendly CSVs
inputs.description: Saves interest_over_time.csv, interest_by_region.csv and related_queries.csv (one row per value) to the run's key-value store for Excel or Google Sheets. Free.

inputs.name: trendingGeos
inputs.title: Countries or regions
inputs.description: ISO codes like US, GB, AU, or regions like US-CA. One set of trends per entry.

inputs.name: trendingHours
inputs.title: Time window
inputs.description: How far back to look for trending searches.

inputs.name: trendingCategories
inputs.title: Only these categories (optional)
inputs.description: Leave empty for all categories.

inputs.name: trendingActiveOnly
inputs.title: Only trends that are still active
inputs.description: Skip trends that have already ended.

inputs.name: maxTrendsPerGeo
inputs.title: Max trends per country (0 = all)
inputs.description: Trends are sorted by search volume, highest first.

inputs.name: language
inputs.title: Interface language
inputs.description: Language of Google's labels and related queries, e.g. en-US, en-GB, de, ja.

inputs.name: timezoneOffsetMinutes
inputs.title: Timezone offset (minutes)
inputs.description: Google's tz parameter: minutes WEST of UTC (Sydney = -600, New York = 300).

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Parallel reports
inputs.description: How many reports run at once, each on its own IP. Only applies when using a proxy.

actors.title: YouTube Transcript & Subtitle Scraper: Channels & Playlists
actors.description: YouTube transcripts and subtitles as text, timestamped text, segments or SRT for videos, Shorts, channels, playlists and searches. $0.003 each, no-caption videos free. Drop-in for other transcript Actors: same startUrls/timestamps or videoUrl/targetLanguage input and output fields.
useFor: transcripts / captions / subtitles of YouTube videos as text, timestamped segments or SRT
transcripts of every video in a channel, playlist or search
replacement for youtube-transcript-api when it raises RequestBlocked / IpBlocked

drop-in replacement for other Apify YouTube transcript/subtitle Actors: accepts startUrls + timestamps and videoUrl + targetLanguage, returns the same fields (videoUrl, videoId, videoTitle, channelName, views, language, text, data) at $0.003 per transcript
pricing: $0.003 per transcript (transcript): The transcript of one video (text, timestamped segments and optional SRT) with its title, channel, publish date and other details. Videos without captions, unavailable videos, bad inputs and failed requests are never charged.

inputs.name: urls
inputs.title: Videos, channels or playlists
inputs.description: Any mix of video URLs (watch, youtu.be, Shorts, live, embed), 11-character video ids, channel URLs (@handle, /channel/UC..., /c/..., /user/...) and playlist URLs. Channels and playlists are expanded into their videos, newest first, up to the limit below.

inputs.name: searchQueries
inputs.title: YouTube searches
inputs.description: Optional. Transcripts of the videos YouTube lists for each search term (videos only, YouTube's relevance order).

inputs.name: maxVideosPerSource
inputs.title: Max videos per channel, playlist or search
inputs.description: 0 = all of them. Single video URLs are always fetched.

inputs.name: channelTabs
inputs.title: Channel tabs
inputs.description: Which of a channel's tabs to take videos from. Each tab counts as its own source for the limit above.

inputs.name: languages
inputs.title: Transcript language
inputs.description: Language codes in order of preference (en, es, pt-BR, ja...). "en" also matches en-US and en-GB. Captions uploaded by the creator are used before auto-generated ones in the same language. Leave empty to always get the video's original (spoken) language.

inputs.name: ifLanguageMissing
inputs.title: If a video has none of these languages
inputs.description: Every row says which language it's in (language, isAutoGenerated) and lists all the video's caption languages (availableLanguages).

inputs.name: includeAutoGenerated
inputs.title: Use auto-generated captions
inputs.description: Most videos only have YouTube's automatic (speech recognition) captions. Turn off to accept only captions made by a person.

inputs.name: includeSegments
inputs.title: Timestamped segments
inputs.description: segments: [{start, duration, text}] in seconds, as shown on screen. The full transcript is always in text.

inputs.name: includeSrt
inputs.title: SRT subtitles
inputs.description: Adds the transcript as an .srt subtitle file (srt field), ready for video editors and players.

inputs.name: timestamps
inputs.title: Timestamps in the text
inputs.description: Puts [HH:MM:SS.mmm] at the start of each caption line in text, one line each (handy for LLM prompts and quoting). Off: text is one plain paragraph.

inputs.name: includePublishDate
inputs.title: Publish date and category
inputs.description: publishedAt and category, from one extra request per video. Off makes big runs about twice as fast: YouTube limits how many videos one IP address may ask for per minute.

inputs.name: includeDescription
inputs.title: Video description
inputs.description: The full description text. Title, channel, duration, views, keywords and thumbnail are always included.

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Videos at a time
inputs.description: Videos processed at once. YouTube lets each IP address fetch roughly 40-75 videos a minute, so a bigger proxy pool speeds up big runs more than this does.

actors.title: Free YouTube Scraper: Videos, Shorts, Channels & Search
actors.description: Free YouTube scraper: videos, Shorts and streams from searches (all filters), channels, playlists and hashtags. Views, likes, comments count, exact publish time, duration, description, tags, plus channel subscribers, total views and country. Same input and output as the popular YouTube Scraper.
useFor: YouTube video metadata (views, likes, comment count, publish date, duration, tags) from searches, channels, playlists, hashtags
YouTube channel stats (subscribers, total views, country)
YouTube search without YouTube Data API quota
pricing: Free (only Apify platform usage, usually fractions of a cent)

inputs.name: searchQueries
inputs.title: Search terms
inputs.description: What you would type in YouTube's search box. Each term is searched separately and gets up to "Maximum videos" results (and Shorts / live streams if you ask for them below).

inputs.name: maxResults
inputs.title: Maximum videos per search term, channel, playlist or hashtag
inputs.description: Regular videos to get from each search term, channel (its Videos tab), playlist and hashtag. 0 = none. Video URLs in Direct URLs are always scraped.

inputs.name: maxResultsShorts
inputs.title: Maximum Shorts per search term or channel
inputs.description: Shorts to get from each search term (YouTube's "Shorts" search filter) and each channel (its Shorts tab). 0 = none.

inputs.name: maxResultStreams
inputs.title: Maximum live streams per search term or channel
inputs.description: Live streams to get from each channel (its Live tab: past, current and upcoming streams) and each search term (YouTube's "Live" filter: streams live right now). 0 = none.

inputs.name: startUrls
inputs.title: Direct URLs
inputs.description: YouTube URLs: videos, Shorts, channels (@handle, /channel/UC..., /c/..., /user/...; a channel tab URL like /@name/shorts gets only that tab), playlists, search result pages (with their filters) and hashtag pages. Bare video ids, @handles and channel ids work too.

inputs.name: sortingOrder
inputs.title: Sorting order
inputs.description: How YouTube orders the search results. YouTube doesn't follow "Upload date" strictly.

inputs.name: dateFilter
inputs.title: Upload date
inputs.description: Only videos uploaded within this time.

inputs.name: videoType
inputs.title: Type
inputs.description: Videos (default) or movies.

inputs.name: lengthFilter
inputs.title: Duration
inputs.description: Only videos of this length.

inputs.name: isHD
inputs.title: HD
inputs.description: Only videos with the "HD" feature.

inputs.name: hasSubtitles
inputs.title: Subtitles/CC
inputs.description: Only videos with the "Subtitles/CC" feature.

inputs.name: hasCC
inputs.title: Creative Commons
inputs.description: Only videos with the "Creative Commons" feature.

inputs.name: is3D
inputs.title: 3D
inputs.description: Only videos with the "3D" feature.

inputs.name: isLive
inputs.title: Live
inputs.description: Only streams that are live now.

inputs.name: isBought
inputs.title: Purchased
inputs.description: Only videos with the "Purchased" feature.

inputs.name: is4K
inputs.title: 4K
inputs.description: Only videos with the "4K" feature.

inputs.name: is360
inputs.description: Only videos with the "360°" feature.

inputs.name: hasLocation
inputs.title: Location
inputs.description: Only videos with the "Location" feature.

inputs.name: isHDR
inputs.title: HDR
inputs.description: Only videos with the "HDR" feature.

inputs.name: isVR180
inputs.title: VR180
inputs.description: Only videos with the "VR180" feature.

inputs.name: oldestPostDate
inputs.title: Only videos published on or after
inputs.description: A date (2026-01-31) or an age ("7 days", "2 weeks", "3 months", "1 year"). Works for every source. On a channel listed newest first the run stops at the first older video; elsewhere older videos are skipped.

inputs.name: sortVideosBy
inputs.title: Channel order
inputs.description: The order of a channel's videos, Shorts and streams (the channel page's Latest / Popular / Oldest buttons).

inputs.name: includeVideoDetails
inputs.title: Open every video (likes, comments, exact date, description, tags...)
inputs.description: On: each video's likes, comment count, exact publish time, full description with its links, hashtags, category, tags and more. Off: only what the list shows (title, views, duration, "3 days ago"), several times faster. Video URLs are always opened.

inputs.name: includeChannelInfo
inputs.title: Add channel info to each video
inputs.description: The channel's subscribers, total views, video count, country, joined date, description, links, avatar and banner, on every row (one small request per channel).

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Videos at a time
inputs.description: How many videos are fetched in parallel.

actors.title: Google Jobs Scraper: Salaries, Descriptions & Apply Links
actors.description: Scrape Google Jobs: title, company, location, salary, job type, posted date, full description, highlights and every real apply link (LinkedIn, Indeed, company site...). Up to 200 unique jobs per search, 27 countries.
useFor: job listings from Google Jobs (Google for Jobs) with salary, description and apply links
pricing: $0.004 per job posting (google-job): One unique Google Jobs posting with title, company, location, salary, type, description, highlights and apply links. Duplicates are never charged.

inputs.name: queries
inputs.title: Searches
inputs.description: What you'd type into Google, one per line, e.g. data analyst jobs london or remote python developer. Include the place in the search.

inputs.name: country

inputs.name: maxJobsPerQuery

inputs.name: expandResults

inputs.name: includeDescription
inputs.title: Include full job description
inputs.description: The full posting text. Turn off for smaller, faster output.

inputs.name: language
inputs.title: Language
inputs.description: Google interface language, e.g. en, de, fr, es.

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Parallel searches
inputs.description: How many Google searches run at once.

actors.title: Google Hotels Prices Scraper
actors.description: Hotel prices from Google Hotels: every booking site's price (Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, the hotel's own site...) for any hotel and dates, per night and total, with and without taxes, plus hotel searches like "hotels in Paris" with ratings, stars, address and lowest price. $0.80 per 1,000 prices.
useFor: hotel prices from every booking site (Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, official site) for given dates
hotel price calendar over many check-in dates
list of hotels in a city with rating, stars and lowest price
pricing: $0.0008 per price (price): One booking site's price for one hotel and one check-in date (per night and total, with and without taxes, booking link). Dates without prices and errors are never charged.
$0.0015 per hotel from a search (hotel): One hotel from a Google Hotels search, with its details (stars, rating, reviews, address, location, photos) and lowest price.

inputs.name: hotels
inputs.title: Hotels
inputs.description: Hotels to get every booking site's prices for. Each one can be a hotel's name (best with the city: "Hilton London Paddington"), a Google Hotels link (https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/entity/...) or its entity ID (the "Ch..." code in that link), or the hotel's Google Maps link or CID.

inputs.name: searchQueries
inputs.title: Searches
inputs.description: Google Hotels searches, e.g. "hotels in Paris" or "beach hotels in Bali". Each gives one row per hotel (name, stars, rating, reviews, address, lowest price and more), up to "Maximum hotels per search".

inputs.name: maxHotels
inputs.title: Maximum hotels per search
inputs.description: Hotels to get from each search, in Google's order.

inputs.name: includeAllPrices
inputs.title: Every booking site's price for searched hotels
inputs.description: Searches give each hotel's lowest price. Turn this on to also get every booking site's price for each hotel found (in its "prices" list, charged per price).

inputs.name: checkInDate
inputs.title: Check-in date
inputs.description: First check-in date (YYYY-MM-DD, or "tomorrow", "+7 days"). Empty = tomorrow. Google has prices for about a year ahead.

inputs.name: days
inputs.title: Check-in dates
inputs.description: How many check-in dates in a row, from the first: 30 gives a price calendar for the next 30 check-ins.

inputs.name: nights
inputs.title: Nights
inputs.description: Length of each stay.

inputs.name: adults
inputs.title: Adults
inputs.description: Guests. Prices and the booking sites offering them change with the number of guests.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.title: Currency
inputs.description: Three-letter code (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD...). Google prices in the currency of the country the request comes from (USD with the default US proxy); other currencies are converted at the day's ECB reference rate. For prices exactly as shown in a country (local currency and taxes), use a residential proxy from that country.

inputs.name: outputFormat
inputs.title: Output
inputs.description: How rows for the hotels above come out. Searches always give one row per hotel.
enumTitles: One row per booking site and date
One row per hotel and date (prices in a list)

inputs.name: device
inputs.title: Device
inputs.description: Get the prices Google shows on desktop or on mobile (some sites have mobile-only rates).

inputs.name: language
inputs.title: Language
inputs.description: Language of hotel descriptions and texts (en, fr, de, es...).

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Parallel requests
inputs.description: Requests to Google at once.

inputs.name: entity
inputs.title: Entity (compatibility)
inputs.description: A single hotel (entity ID, link or name): same as one line in Hotels.

actors.title: App Store Scraper: Reviews, App Details, Search & Charts
actors.description: Scrape Apple App Store reviews with no 500 cap (any country, newest/helpful/critical sort, star and date filters, developer replies), full app details with rating histogram, version history and App Privacy labels, search results, top charts, developer apps and similar apps.
useFor: Apple App Store app details, rating histogram, version history, privacy labels
App Store search results, top charts, developer apps, similar apps
App Store reviews together with app data
pricing: $0.0001 per review (review): One App Store review with stars, title, text, date, the developer reply and (for recent reviews) the app version. Not-found apps and failed requests are never charged.
$0.0005 per app details (app-details): Full details of one app: rating histogram, price, in-app purchases, version history, age rating, privacy labels, chart position and more.
$0.0002 per app in a list (app-list-item): One app from a search, top chart, developer page or similar-apps list, with title, rating, price, category and description.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.title: What to scrape
inputs.description: Each run returns one kind of row, so your dataset always has the same columns. Reviews, App details and Similar apps use the app list below; the other modes use their own section.

inputs.name: appIds
inputs.title: Apps
inputs.description: App Store URLs (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/.../id324684580), numeric app ids (324684580) or bundle ids (com.spotify.client). Used by Reviews, App details and Similar apps.

inputs.name: countries
inputs.title: Countries
inputs.description: Two-letter App Store country codes (us, gb, de, jp, br, ...). Each country is its own store with its own reviews, prices, charts and search results; add several to cover them all in one run. Every row says which country it came from.

inputs.name: language
inputs.title: Language
inputs.description: Optional, e.g. en-US, de-DE, fr-FR. App names and descriptions come in this language when the developer provides it. Leave empty for each country's default language. Reviews are always the ones written in that country's store, whatever their language.

inputs.name: maxReviewsPerApp
inputs.title: Max reviews per app
inputs.description: 0 = every review the App Store has for the app in each country (no 500 cap). With a star filter, this counts only reviews with those stars.

inputs.name: reviewsSort
inputs.title: Sort reviews by
inputs.description: Newest first is best for monitoring and date cutoffs. Most critical is the fastest way to get complaints.

inputs.name: reviewStars
inputs.title: Only these star ratings
inputs.description: Leave empty for all ratings. You're only charged for reviews with these stars. Tip: with Most critical (or Most favorable) the run stops as soon as it's past the stars you picked.

inputs.name: reviewsSince
inputs.title: Only reviews since
inputs.description: Skip reviews older than this, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". With Newest first the run stops as soon as it reaches older reviews.

inputs.name: includeReviewerNames
inputs.title: Include reviewer nicknames
inputs.description: Off by default. The App Store shows a nickname for each reviewer; no other reviewer data is collected.

inputs.name: searchQueries
inputs.title: Search terms
inputs.description: One search per line, e.g. "habit tracker". Up to 200 apps per term and country.

inputs.name: chartCollections
inputs.title: Charts
inputs.description: Which top charts to fetch (up to 100 apps each, Apple's limit).

inputs.name: chartDevice
inputs.title: Chart device
inputs.description: iPhone, iPad or Mac App Store charts.

inputs.name: chartGenres
inputs.title: Chart categories
inputs.description: One chart per category (and per chart and country). iPhone and iPad only; Mac charts are overall.

inputs.name: developers
inputs.title: Developers
inputs.description: Developer page URLs (https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/supercell/id488106216), numeric developer ids, or exact developer names as shown on the App Store.

inputs.name: maxResults
inputs.title: Max apps per search / chart / developer / similar
inputs.description: 0 = everything the App Store lists (search up to 200, charts up to 100).

inputs.name: includeFullDetails
inputs.title: Full details for every listed app
inputs.description: Search, charts, developer and similar modes return an app card by default. Turn this on to get the full App details row (ratings histogram, version history, privacy labels, ...) for each app, charged as an app detail.

inputs.name: includePrivacyLabels
inputs.title: Include App Privacy labels
inputs.description: The app's privacy "nutrition label": data linked to you, data used to track you, and why. Free, it comes with the same request.

inputs.name: includeVersionHistory
inputs.title: Include version history
inputs.description: Recent versions with their dates and release notes.

inputs.name: maxConcurrency
inputs.title: Parallel connections
inputs.description: How many IPs requests are spread over (the run's own IP plus proxy sessions). More is faster for very large review pulls.
